brief_title: Is Insulin Resistance and/or Glucose Intolerance Pathogenetic in the Development of a Reduced Incretin Effect
official_title: Is Insulin Resistance and/or Glucose Intolerance Pathogenetic in the Development of a Reduced Incretin Effect

primary_outcomes.measure: Incremental GLP-1 response during the mixed meal test. Assessed as AUC during the 4 hour test.

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to examine whether there is a causal relationship between insulin resistance and/or glucose intolerance in the development of a defect incretin effect.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Caucasians \>20 years
* Normal glucose tolerance as assessed by the WHO criteria
* First degree relative and at least 1 second degree relative with type 2 diabetes
* Normal haemoglobin
* Informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Liver disease (ALAT/ASAT \> 2 times normal value)
* Kidney disease (S-creatinin \> 130uM and/or albuminuria)
* Heart disease (NYHA II, III or IV)
* Treatment with medicine that cannot be paused
* Pregnancy of breast feeding
